817:
(a) The government of the city is firmly committed to providing its employees with a safe work place and promoting high standards of employee health. Consistent with the spirit and intent of this commitment, the mayor and council have established this policy regarding alcohol and substance abuse. The mayor and council's goal will continue to be one of establishing and maintaining a work environment that is free from the effects of alcohol and substance abuse.
(b) Government has several uniquely compelling interests that justify the implementation of procedures for employee alcohol and substance testing. The public has a right to expect that those who have the responsibility of providing services to taxpayers of the city are at all times both physically and mentally prepared to perform their assigned job duties. There is sufficient evidence to conclude that the use of alcohol and certain substances may seriously impair an employee's physical and mental health, and thus, job performance. Where employees participate in alcohol and substance abuse, the integrity of city government and public confidence therein is destroyed.
(c) The city recognizes that employees have privacy interests and certain privacy rights in their medical condition and treatment. The city respects those interests and rights as long as the privacy of those matters does not impact the safety of the citizens of the city, the safety employees, and the delivery of city services.
(d) Therefore, in order to ensure the integrity of the city's government and to preserve public trust and confidence, the mayor and council hereby implements an alcohol and substance abuse policy and testing program to detect prohibited alcohol and substance use by city employees and those persons performing services on behalf of the city.
(Ord. No. 2002-13, § 30(70-126), 8-19-2002; Ord. No. 2009-04, § 2(70-126), 5-11-2009)
820:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this division, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Alcohol means ethyl alcohol, hydrated oxide of ethyl, or spirits of wine, from whatever source or by whatever process produced. For the purpose of this division, the term "alcohol" shall include distilled spirits, beer, malt beverage or fortified wine.
Chain of custody means procedures to account for the integrity of each specimen by tracking its handling and storage from point of specimen collection to fine disposition of the specimen. These procedures shall not be required to negative any possibility of contamination, but shall ensure to a reasonable certainty that the sample remains identifiable and untainted.
Collection site means the facility or location designated by the city (or any alternate site authorized by this division) where individuals present themselves for the purpose of providing a specimen of their blood, breath or urine to be analyzed for the presence of alcohol or substances.
Collection site person means personnel under the direction of the facility or location staff or personnel employed by any alternate collection site authorized by this division, who will instruct and assist individuals at a collection site and who will receive and make an initial examination of the specimen provided by those individuals. A collection site person shall be familiar with the procedures with collection and preservation of samples of bodily substances.
Confirmatory test means a second analytical procedure to identify the presence of a specific substance or metabolite which is independent of the initial test and which may use a different technique and chemical principle from that of the initial test in order to ensure reliability and accuracy.
Controlled substance means those substances as defined in the state Controlled Substances Act (O.C.G.A. § 16-13-20 et seq.). The term "controlled substance" shall include marijuana as defined by O.C.G.A. § 16-13-21.
Department head means the senior person in a department of the city, supervising the activities of that department.
Employee means those individuals who occupy a position in city government or performing services on behalf of any private or corporate entity on behalf of the city.
Initial test (also known as screening test) means an immunoassay screen to eliminate negative specimens from further consideration.
Permanent record book means a book or log in which identifying data on each specimen collected at a collection site is permanently recorded in the sequence of collection.
Reasonable suspicion means that quantity or proof of evidence that is more than a hunch, but less than probable cause. Reasonable suspicion must be based on specific, objective facts and any rationally derived inferences from those facts about the conduct of an individual that would lead a reasonable person to suspect that the individual is or has been using alcohol or controlled substances while on or off duty.
Test, alcohol or substance, means the compulsory production and submission of blood, breath or urine by an employee in accordance with city government procedures for chemical analysis to detect prohibited alcohol and/or substance usage.
(Ord. No. 2002-13, § 33(70-136), 8-19-2002; Ord. No. 2009-04, § 4(70-136), 5-11-2009)
821:
(a) Except as hereafter provided, the use, possession, sale, distribution or provision of alcohol or any controlled substance during work time or on the work premises shall be prohibited. This provision shall not apply to employees when such use, possession, sale, distribution or provision of alcohol or any controlled substance is an incident to the employees' lawful duties or is otherwise required in the normal course of their employment.
(b) Reporting to work or working while under the influence or otherwise impaired by alcohol or any controlled substance shall be prohibited.
(c) Alcohol or controlled substance-related off-duty use that tends to undermine the reputation, authority or efficiency of the city government is prohibited.
(d) The use or possession of prescription drugs while on the work premises or while working shall be prohibited unless the prescription container does not have a warning that the contents should not be used when operating equipment or motor vehicles, may cause drowsiness, or any other warning that may describe a reaction to the contents that would reasonably be expected to impair the ability of the employee to perform his duties safely and effectively. If such a warning was on the prescription container when filled, then the employee shall ensure that:
(1) The prescribing physician has been notified of the duties involved with the employee's position and has approved the use of the drug while that employee is performing those duties; and
(2) The employee's immediate supervisor has been notified in writing by the employee that he is using a prescription drug and that the employee's physician has approved the use of the drug while the employee is at work.
(Ord. No. 2002-13, § 34(70-137), 8-19-2002; Ord. No. 2009-04, § 4(70-137), 5-11-2009)
822:
(a) Alcohol and/or substance testing may be required of job applicants for positions which deal with public safety; or which require or permit the use of motor vehicles or heavy equipment; or which would pose a threat of bodily harm to the applicant; coworkers or the general public if the applicant was impaired. Whether a particular position comes within the meaning of this section will be determined by the city manager in consultation with the department head, or at the direction of the mayor. At the time applications for any position covered by this section are received, the applicant will be informed that employment is conditional upon alcohol or substance testing. The term "applicant" shall include any current employee of the city that is applying for any position covered by this section as well as any person not a current employee of the city.
(b) Alcohol and/or substance testing will be required of employees for which reasonable suspicion exists to believe that such employees are under the influence of alcohol or substances during assigned working hours or while otherwise on city property. Testing may be required following work-related accidents if the surrounding circumstances give rise to reasonable suspicion to believe that such employees are under the influence of alcohol or substances.
(1) The initial determination of whether or not reasonable suspicion exists shall be made by the department head or by the highest ranking supervisory staff person on duty at the time. The department head or supervisory staff person shall consult with the city manager (or city clerk in the absence of the city manager), when available, for the purpose of determining if an alcohol or substance test is appropriate under the circumstances.
(2) Following the determination that reasonable suspicion exists and an alcohol or substance test should be administered, the employee shall be immediately transported to the collection site by the employee's department head or such designee of the department director. Following the collection procedure, the person transporting the employee shall make appropriate arrangements to transport the employee home.
(3) Public safety department heads and their designees shall not be required to consult with the city manager prior to making a determination that reasonable suspicion exists, inasmuch as those individuals and their designees have specific training qualifying them to make such determinations. Accordingly, when a public safety department head or designee makes the determination that reasonable suspicion exists, the employee shall be immediately transported to the collection site as is provided hereinabove.
(4) Any employee tested under this provision may be suspended without pay for up to three days pending the results of the test. If the results of the test are negative, the employee shall return to work with complete restoration of lost salary.
(Ord. No. 2002-13, § 35(70-138), 8-19-2002; Ord. No. 2009-04, § 4(70-138), 5-11-2009)
